summary: Ulrich Schneider (1922–1992) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig under Friedrich Weller, later serving as an assistant there, followed by professorial posts at Freiburg and Münster.

Ulrich Timme Kragh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and Karmapa International Buddhist Institute. His posts include positions at Copenhagen, Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, Sydney, and ANU.

Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff (1848–1931) was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Schulpforta, Bonn, and Berlin under Schmidt, Jahn, and Haupt, and held professorships at the universities of Greifswald, Göttingen, and Berlin.

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She received her PhD from the University of Münster, taught at Marburg and Freiburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at the University of Oxford.

Uma Chakravarti is a historian and scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor D. Devahuti, and served as an educator at Miranda House from 1966 to 1998.

Umakant Premanand Shah (1915–1988) was an Indologist and historian. He served as deputy director and head of the Ramayana Project at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, and was director at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1954–1975).

Umar Rolf von Ehrenfels (1901–1980) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna and served as Head of Anthropology at the University of Madras and guest professor at Heidelberg.
Umberto Norsa (1866–1943) was an Indology scholar who completed law studies at the University of Bologna (~1884–1888) and served as secretary at the Gabinetto di Lettura di Mantova from 1893 to 1938.

Umesh Kumar Singh is an Indologist. He earned a B.A. from the University of Allahabad (1997–2000), an M.A. from Banaras Hindu University (2000–2002), and a Ph.D. from the University of Delhi (2004–2010).

Umesha Mishra (1895–1967) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp. He held posts at the University of Allahabad, Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha, and the Mithila Institute.

Unapane Pemananda specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at USN, Oslo, Peradeniya, and the University of Hong Kong (PhD). His posts include the University of Oslo (2025) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana works in Indology and related fields. He earned degrees from Bharathiar University, Amsterdam, and Yokohama National University. He held positions at FRLHT, University of Toyama, United Nations University, and TDU.

Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann and Junjirō Takakusu, and held positions at Shukyo University, the University of Tokyo, and Taisho University as Professor of Sanskrit.
Unsho Shaku (1827–1909) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded the Juze-kai (1884), Kairitsu Gakko, and Juuzen Hokutsu.

Unuwaturabubule Mahinda works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura and studied at Kelaniya. He has held teaching posts at Sri Jayewardenepura, Buddhist and Pali University of Sri Lanka, and PGIPBS.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. at SOAS University of London and held a post as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at UC Berkeley and held positions at Mongolian National University of Arts and Culture, UC Berkeley, National University of Mongolia, Yonsei, and Herron/IUPUI.

Uranchimeg Tsultemin is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She received her Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley, where she worked as a lecturer, and served as an Associate Professor at the National University of Mongolia.

Urs App is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Temple University, studying under Victor H. Mair. He held posts at Hanazono University, the Swiss National Science Foundation, and EFEO.
Usha Nilsson (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who served as a faculty member and Emeritus Professor of Languages and Cultures of Asia at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
